givemotion: judge-1 (as A): It hits most beats. The knockout type shows the coral spine through the 'K' (1.56–2.3s), the downward wipe to YOU NEED / ONE. is clean (2.3–2.5s), and the tracking widens on 594.56 (7.0–7.7s). The final frame (23.8s) is the strongest of the three: wide type with a neat coral underline. The band-to-spine handover breaks down: at 15.94s OCTOPUSES is clipped under a sliding slate band, and at 16.2s there is a squat coral block with a stray mustard ',000' counter fragment mid-frame. The coral dot sits in the second floor-plan row, not the fifth (17.1s), and the opening type is well under the full-width 250 px the brief asks for.

judge-2 (as A): Strong opening: the spine wall stays visible through the knockout 'A MILLION / BOOKS.' (2.0s), the wipe down to 'YOU NEED / ONE.' is clean (2.3–2.5s), and at 3.8s the camera pushes into the spine and its label grows into the card. Its outro type is the closest to the brief, at about 190 px and full width with a neat underline at 23.8s. The Beat 2 headline is small for the space, and the Beat 3 to 4 handover is messy: at 16.2s a cut-off ',000' from the counter floats under a half-built wall, with the coral block hanging below the shelf line. The band re-splits at 12.6–12.9s read as tidy but mechanical.

judge-3 (as B): Beat 1 is the strongest of the three: the knockout 'A MILLION / BOOKS.' at 2.0s shows the live wall through the letters, with shelves still visible above and below. The final card at 23.8s fills the width with confident, large Bebas type, and the 3.8s push into the spine is good. The beat 3→4 handover breaks down. At 15.94s the OCTOPUSES text is clipped as the bands scroll, and at 16.2s a stray masked counter fragment (',000') floats mid-frame next to a squat coral block instead of a tall spine. The re-split at 12.7–12.9s looks scattered rather than staggered left to right.

judge-4 (as C): Clearest wall-to-card hand-off, with a visible push into the coral spine and its label at 3.8s. The knockout shows the most wall at 1.56–2.3s, the ADDRESS size step adds hierarchy, and the outro is the strongest end frame: large, justified to the margins, with the ribbon settling at 23.8s. The re-split brings slate bands back in jagged pieces (9.69s, 12.6–12.9s), words fade in from grey at 17.3s and 17.7s instead of snapping, and the rebuild at 15.94–16.2s is cluttered, with OCTOPUSES cut off and the counter still half-rolled.

judge-5 (as B): The strongest handover is the real camera push into the coral spine at 3.8s, and the knockout 'BOOKS.' with the coral spine showing through the K (2.0s) is a smart use of the shared element. Bands expand with the category name still inside and re-split in a clean stagger (12.3–12.9s), and the outro type is large, fills the margins and ends with a confident underline (23.8–24.7s). Weak points: the Beat 3→4 handover, where OCTOPUSES is half cut off at 15.94s and 16.2s is mostly empty with a stray counter fragment rolling out, and the floor-plan dot sits mid-row rather than at the labelled end.

judge-6 (as C): The best push-in of the three: at 3.8s we sit inside the coral spine with its label about to grow. The outro type is also the strongest, large and full width with a confident underline (23.8s). The paper-edged wipe at 2.3–2.5s and the bigger ADDRESS for hierarchy (5.3s) show care. But the middle is untidy: band transitions at 9.69s leave a floating '5' and stacked Slate scraps, and the re-split at 12.7–12.9s rebuilds from the middle in odd fragments. At 15.94s the OCTOPUSES label is clipped, and at 16.2s the frame is mostly empty with a cut-off ',000' counter fragment. The floor-plan headline words fade in grey (17.3–17.7s) where the brief asks for hard snaps.
remotion: judge-1 (as B): It has the best shared-element continuity. The 3.8s push-in already shows the label reading 594.56 as it grows into the Beat 2 card, and at 16.2s the shelf wall rebuilds around the returning coral spine in the middle row, which is the clearest match cut of the three. The counter visibly scrolls between values (10.0s, 11.56s) and the bands wipe out and re-split with a clear stagger (12.5–12.9s). Weaknesses: the closing type is noticeably smaller than 190 px and doesn't fill the width (23.8s), the bar runs ahead of its reveal edge (22.6–22.9s), the dot is in the wrong row (17.1s), and the knockout panel hides most of the wall in Beat 1 (1.56s).

judge-2 (as C): Best continuity: at 3.8s the camera pushes into the coral spine while the label, already showing 594.56, grows. At 16.2s the shelf wall rebuilds cleanly around the spine, and the counter rolls as digits scroll (10.0s, 11.56s). The knockout uses a full-frame ink panel, which follows the brief literally, but the wall disappears for all of 1.2–3.2s, which is less rich. A block typing cursor appears on 'DEWEY…' (5.94s, 6.56s), which is an extra glyph the copy list forbids. The dot sits in the aisle rather than on its row (17.1s), and the outro type is around 130 px rather than 190.

judge-3 (as A): This has the most faithful shared-element chain. At 3.8s the camera push lands the coral spine's label as the 594.56 card, and at 16.2s the wall rebuilds cleanly with the spine back in its original slot. The level wipes and re-splits at 12.3–12.9s are orderly, and the counter roll at 10.0s ('1 IN 10' rolling up) and the decimal pulse at 12.7s are both visible. Weaknesses: 15.94s mixes leftover bands with half-built shelf rows. The outro type (22–24s) and the beat-2 headline are well under the specified size, so the final card feels small in the vertical frame.

judge-4 (as A): Its knockout is a true Ink-panel cut-out, though the letters read dim and muddy at 1.56–2.1s. The push-in at 3.8s, the clean wall rebuild at 16.2s and the crisp counter rolls (10.0s, 11.56s) are strengths. The re-split steps slate bands back in instead of drawing divider lines (9.69s, 12.6–12.9s), and the headline at 4.69–7.8s and outro type at 23.8s are smaller than the brief asks. In the outro sweep the bar runs ahead of its reveal edge (22.6–23.0s).

judge-5 (as C): Best Beat 1→2 match cut: at 3.8s the spine fills the frame and its label already reads 594.56. The full-frame knockout panel (1.56–2.4s), the visible counter roll (10.0s) and the clean wall rebuild at 16.2s all follow the brief closely. Minuses: a block typing cursor after 'DEWEY…' (5.94–6.56s) adds an off-copy glyph, the rebuilt spine straddles a shelf line instead of landing where it started (16.2s), the floor-plan dot sits in the aisle rather than on its row (17.2s), and the outro type is smaller than B's.

judge-6 (as B): The most complete and controlled piece. True knockout over a full Ink panel, with the coral spine showing through the K (1.56–2.2s). A real camera push at 3.8s, where the spine fills the frame with its label already becoming the 594.56 card. A visible left wipe of the headline at 7.8s, readable vertical counter rolls (10.0s), a decimal pulse at 12.7s, and a clean rebuild of the wall around the spine at 16.2–16.56s. Weaknesses: the typing cursor block at 5.94–6.56s is an extra mark not in the copy list, and stray Paper wipe lines sit at the frame top at 17.1–17.2s. The knockout letters are low in contrast, and the band re-split at 12.6–12.9s is a wipe back to Slate rather than the clean divider lines the brief asks for.
hyperframes: judge-1 (as C): It has the same structure and correct copy and palette, with a good wall build (0.31–0.94s), the knockout coral 'L' (1.56–2.2s), and line-by-line divider draws on the re-split (12.6–12.9s). It has the most visible errors: MOLLUSKS is cropped at the top by its band mask during the expand (12.4s), coral slivers are left on bands 8–9 (12.0s), and the label card simply vanishes, leaving a greyed number floating (7.9s). The 16.2s handover is a cluttered pile of half-gone bands, white lines and partly rebuilt spines with a stray band digit, so the spine never reads as landing back in place. The outro bar overshoots toward the right edge (22.9s) and the opening type is undersized.

judge-2 (as B): Same structure as the others, with a good knockout over a visible wall at 2.0s and clean divider lines drawing across the full coral stack at 10.0s and 12.6–12.9s. The push into the spine reaches a blank coral field with an empty card by 3.8s, so the label-to-card match cut is not visible. The worst frame of the three is at 16.2s: slate bands, white shelf lines, a wide coral bar and rebuilding spines all pile up, and the digit '9' shows through the books. In the outro the coral bar runs ahead of the revealed text (22.5–22.9s), so it does not read as the wipe edge, the type is smaller than the brief asks, and 'MOLLUSKS' is clipped at 12.4s.

judge-3 (as C): The knockout wall at 2.0s is solid, and the re-split divider lines at 12.6–12.9s are the cleanest of the three: true left-to-right staggered draws. The outro sweep at 22–23s is tidy. But the category names vanish as soon as each band starts to grow (MOLLUSKS is clipped at 12.4s), and the full-frame coral fields at 9.69, 11.56 and 12.81s are empty and read as abstract. The 16.2s handover is the messiest moment in any of the videos: the docked number, bands 0–3, the shelf lines, a wide coral bar and a half-built wall row overlap, with the digit 9 sitting on the books. A late ÷10 also appears after the plan has dimmed at 20.31s.

judge-4 (as B): Best match to the brief on the re-split: divider lines draw across the coral field at 10.0s and 12.6–12.9s, and the knockout over the wall reads well at 2.0–2.2s. The hand-off arrives early and empty, with a blank card on coral at 3.8s, the number typing on at 4.06s and no visible push-in. The number goes muddy grey as it docks at 7.9s, 16.2s is a cluttered mess of broken bands, stray shelf lines and a half-built wall, and a '÷10' sits at the frame edge at 20.31s.

judge-5 (as A): Full structure with neat path drawing and ÷10 pops (17.4–17.9s) and a clean slanted bar-sweep outro (22.0–22.9s). But the 3.8s card is blank and only a partial '5' shows at 4.06s, so the match cut doesn't carry the number. Category names are cut off the moment the band expands (12.4s), and 16.2s is a messy handover frame with leftover bands, Paper rules and a half-built wall overlapping. The lifted number turns muddy grey at 7.9s, and the headline and outro type are under-scaled.

judge-6 (as A): Follows the brief closely: knockout type over the wall at 1.56–2.2s, a clean downward wipe to YOU NEED / ONE. at 2.3s, divider lines drawing across the filled band at 12.6–12.9s, and a good bar-sweep outro that ends in an underline at 23.8s. The handovers are weak. At 3.8s there is just a flat coral field with an empty card and no visible push into the spine. At 7.8–7.9s the headline vanishes rather than wiping out, and the lifted number goes a muddy grey on coral. At 16.2s the frame is a mess of gapped bands, stray Paper lines and a wall row overlapping band 9. The small type (DEWEY label, 590–599) is tiny, and the headline hierarchy is flat.
